seen_animation: Frames 1-8: a black line drawing of a shovel lies still across the middle of the frame, triangular grip at lower left, a single thin line for the handle running up-right, and a five-sided blade with a short collar tick at upper right; grey scribbles of grass and twigs fill the background and do not move. Frame 9: a black-outlined lower leg and shoe enters from the top edge and stops just above the top-left corner of the blade. Frame 10: the shoe is planted on the ground just left of the blade, the leg slanting up to the top edge. Frame 11: the same leg stands; a small curved fragment (the sole of a second foot) appears cut off at the top right edge. Frame 12: the planted leg is still left of the blade and a second shoe appears raised at upper left. Frames 13-14: two legs stand side by side in the left half of the frame, shoes on the ground, both left of the blade; the shovel is unchanged. Frame 15: the two legs stay; small jagged black marks appear at the top-left edge. Frame 16: a long narrow wedge with a zigzag lower end comes down between and over the left leg, ending just above the handle, apparently a hand reaching down; its lines cross and double the left leg outline.
seen_film: A shovel lies on dry, straw-covered ground, handle running from lower left up to the blade at upper right; frames 1-8 show it untouched with a static camera. Frame 9: a person's foot in grey trousers swings in from the top, blurred, above the blade. Frame 10: the boot is planted just left of the blade. Frame 11: the leg stands there and a second leg/shadow appears at upper right. Frame 12: the planted foot stays and the other foot is lifted at upper left. Frames 13-14: both boots stand on the ground in the left half of the frame, left of and behind the blade. Frame 15: a hand begins to come down from the top left between the legs. Frame 16: a bare arm and hand reach down to the middle of the handle, about to grab it.
named_subject: A shovel lying on the ground (with a person's legs and hand added as the walker who approaches it and reaches for it).
evidence: Judged from still frames only, not playback. Frames 1-8: shovel position, angle and stillness match film frames 1-8. Frames 9-14: shoe entry above the blade (9), planting left of the blade (10), second foot at upper right (11), raised foot at upper left (12), and two standing legs at left (13-14) match the film's positions and timing closely. Frame 15: the incoming hand is only a few jagged marks at the top edge, much less readable than the film's hand. Frame 16: the reaching hand is drawn as a narrow spike with a zigzag tip that overlaps the left leg so its lines double the leg, and it stops above the handle without touching it, while in film frame 16 a clear hand reaches down onto the middle of the handle. The final event of the shot, the person reaching for the shovel, does not read.
primary_gap: The reaching hand in frames 15-16 is a jagged spike tangled with the left leg and does not reach the handle, so the shot's final action (reaching down to pick up the shovel) is not legible.
closes_when: In frames 15-16 a separate arm-and-hand outline descends from the top left in front of the legs without crossing their lines, and by frame 16 its open fingers sit on the middle of the handle near the same spot as in film frame 16.
protect: The shovel drawn exactly in the doodle's construction (triangle grip, single-line handle, five-sided blade with collar tick) and held still in the film's position; the leg/shoe entry, planting and stride timing in frames 9-14 matching the film; the static grey scenery; plain sparse line style with no shading.
identity_gap: The shovel keeps the doodle's triangle grip, single thin handle and angular five-sided blade with collar tick, only rotated to the film's angle, so it reads as the same drawing.
